bug_semantics: The tRPC report.get procedure in packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts accepted only reportId and returned getReportById(reportId) with no project membership check. enforceAccess in packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts consults membership only when the raw input contains projectId or organizationId, so a reportId-only payload bypassed that middleware. getReportById in packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts does an unscoped Prisma findUnique on the report id. Any authenticated user could therefore read another tenant's full saved-report configuration (projectId, series, filters, breakdowns, formulas). Adjacent update/delete/duplicate procedures already resolved the report and called getProjectAccess on its projectId; the omission was specific to get.
flaw_origin: PR #211 squash 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d first landed report.get on main, but that squash is not the BIC. Reconstructing the 44 public member commits of Openpanel-dev/openpanel#211, git log -S 'return getReportById(reportId)' on packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts between base 436e81ecc9159fd3f2849d538f2122d92342e042 and PR head 330321405d2ba207cb1672d1d38a4f0cdac85ad8 identifies 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec (subject wip) as the smallest commit that first wrote get: protectedProcedure with input {reportId} and return getReportById(reportId). Its parent 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823 already had report.ts with access-checked update/delete and the unscoped getReportById helper, but no get procedure. Later member 6b2efdd19bb044be0c7d0bdde9db0a599cbe2466 only appended updateLayout after the already-vulnerable get. The helper's lack of project scoping is pre-existing; the new IDOR surface is the unchecked report.get endpoint.
